question: What must this page do for its visitors, how well does it do that today, and what must its redesign keep, fix and add?
overall_question: What state is the site in across these pages, how far should the redesign go, and what must the new design system deliver?

scoring.rule: 0 to 100, weighted by each check's weight: pass counts fully, warn a quarter, fail nothing, n/a not at all. Each failed must-have (weight 3) then multiplies the score by 0.8.

checks.question: Is it clear within the first screen what this page offers and for whom?
checks.how: Look at the first screen only: the top 800 px of the desktop screenshot, and on the phone what fits in 844 px (on a shrunk page, divide by its measured scale). Pass: the offer and the audience are obvious without scrolling. Fail: a visitor has to read or scroll to find out.

checks.question: Can visitors complete their top tasks on this page?
checks.how: Name the top tasks (in 'tasks'), then walk through each one on the page. Pass: every task can be completed or clearly continued. Evidence: the task that gets stuck and where.

checks.question: Does the page have everything a visitor needs to decide or act?
checks.how: For this kind of page, list what a visitor expects (prices, steps, deadlines, conditions, contact, opening hours). Fail when something essential is missing; put each gap in 'add'.

checks.question: Is the information current?
checks.how: Look for dates, years, prices, laws, names, old terms, dead offers. Quote anything outdated. Pass when nothing is visibly out of date.

checks.question: Is the text easy to read?
checks.how: Read it, with the measured paragraph and sentence lengths as a guide. Warn: long paragraphs or jargon. Fail: walls of text a visitor won't read.

checks.question: Is the text free of spelling and grammar errors?
checks.how: Quote every error you find, with the correction.

checks.question: Is the content unique to this page?
checks.how: Compare with the other copied pages (content/*.md), leaving out the header, menu and footer every page shares. Warn when blocks repeat elsewhere; name the pages. Repeated blocks are candidates for a shared component.

checks.question: Does the page have exactly one meaningful H1?
checks.how: Pass: one H1 with text (H1s marked aria-hidden don't count). Fail: none, several, or an empty one.

checks.question: Do the headings follow in order without skipping levels?
checks.how: Warn when a level is skipped (h1 to h3) or the first heading is not an H1. Headings in nav, aside and footer don't count.

checks.question: Can a visitor scan the page and find the most important things first?
checks.how: Headings, lists and short blocks; the most important content at the top. Evidence: the block that should come first, or the section that buries its point.

checks.question: Is there one clear main action for this page?
checks.how: Name the action this page should lead to (call, form, booking, download). Pass: it is visible and looks like an action. Fail: none, or several that compete.

checks.question: Is an action (phone link, button, form) visible in the first mobile screen?
checks.how: Pass: a tel: link, a button (or a link styled as one: a btn/button/cta class, or its own background or border, and padding, outside the menu) or a form field inside the first 390 × 844 px (menu and language toggles, select menus and cookie banners don't count). Fail otherwise.

checks.question: Are phone and email clickable?
checks.how: Pass: a tel: or mailto: link. Warn: a phone number (after 'Tel', 'Telefon', 'Telephone', 'Phone' or 'Fon') or an email is shown, but none of that kind is clickable. Fail: no phone number or email on the page.

checks.question: Does the menu show the main sections clearly, with the current page marked?
checks.how: Look at the menu in the screenshots and in the copy (the current page's link is often href="#"). Evidence: missing or unclear sections, no current-page marker, menu hidden in a header image.

checks.question: Does the menu fit and work at phone width?
checks.how: Fail when the visible navigation runs past the right edge of a 390 px screen (menus moved off screen don't count).

checks.question: Do links say where they go?
checks.how: Warn for links whose whole text is 'hier', 'mehr', 'weiter', 'click here', 'more' or similar.

checks.question: Does the page declare a mobile viewport?
checks.how: Fail without <meta name=viewport width=device-width>: phones then show a shrunk desktop page.

checks.question: Does the page fit the phone screen without scrolling sideways?
checks.how: Fail when the page is wider than 390 px at phone width and can be scrolled sideways, or when its viewport says device-width but it is laid out more than 10 % wider and shrunk to fit. Evidence: the measured width.

checks.question: Is body text at least 16 px on phones?
checks.how: Fail below 14 px, warn below 16 px (the most used body text size at 390 px, after the browser's scaling, where a page laid out at most 10 % wider than the phone counts at its own size; fine print in footers, footnotes and <small> doesn't count).

checks.question: Are links and buttons big enough to tap?
checks.how: Links, buttons and form fields narrower or lower than 24 px on the phone screen with another target closer than 24 px (WCAG 2.2 target size); on a shrunk page every small one counts; links inside running text don't (WCAG exempts them). Warn from 3, fail from 10.

checks.question: Are logo, colors and type recognisable and worth keeping?
checks.how: Look at the measured colors, fonts and logo, and the screenshots. Say what is brand (keep) and what is just old (replace). Fail when there is no recognisable identity or it is in poor shape (e.g. a pixelated logo).

checks.question: Are the images sharp, relevant and good enough for a modern page?
checks.how: Use the measured upscaled and broken images, and look at them. Images set as CSS backgrounds aren't measured: check their pixel size in scraped/assets/. Evidence: which images are too small, generic or unrelated.

checks.question: Does the layout guide the eye to what matters?
checks.how: Look at the desktop screenshot: size, weight, spacing and color show what is important. Evidence: what competes or what is lost.

checks.question: Does the page look like the other pages of the site?
checks.how: Compare with the other screenshots. Warn on a different logo, colors or layout.

checks.question: Does text have enough contrast?
checks.how: WCAG AA: 4.5:1, 3:1 for large text. Counted by colour pair (text on background): warn for 1–2 pairs below it, fail from 3. Text over images, photos under it or painted backgrounds can't be measured: n/a when that is all the text.

checks.question: Do images have alt text?
checks.how: Warn when content images have no alt attribute.

checks.question: Does the page declare its language?
checks.how: Fail without <html lang>.

checks.question: Is the page built with current techniques?
checks.how: The modernization score of the HTML and CSS (media queries, flex or grid, no layout tables, no legacy markup). Pass from 70, warn from 40.

checks.question: Is the page light enough?
checks.how: Measured while copying. Warn above 2 MB or 80 requests, fail above 5 MB.

checks.question: Does the page load quickly?
checks.how: Measured while copying (load event). Warn above 2.5 s, fail above 5 s.

checks.question: Is the page served over HTTPS?
checks.how: Fail on http.

checks.question: Does the page have its own, descriptive title?
checks.how: Warn when the title is missing, shorter than 15 or longer than 65 characters, or the same on other pages.

checks.question: Does the page have a meta description?
checks.how: Warn when there is neither a meta description nor an og:description.

checks.question: Does the page give visitors reasons to trust the business?
checks.how: Credentials, audits and ratings, team, years in business, references, real photos. Evidence: what is there and what is missing; missing items go to 'add'.

checks.question: Are imprint and privacy policy linked?
checks.how: Pass when the page links to both (Impressum/Imprint and Datenschutz/Privacy); on English pages a privacy link is enough.
